script.base: WAS -5.5 at home in a 40.5 total (implied WAS 23.0 / PHI 17.5), wind 5.1 and 49.6°F so no weather drag. PHI, with Tanner McKee at QB, trails and is forced to throw: WAS blitzes 46% and PHI EPA/db is -0.23 vs blitz (vs -0.03 unblitzed), so the PHI pass game funnels short/middle to Dallas Goedert (24 tgt / 147 yds) and Makai Lemon (21/129) rather than deep to DeVonta Smith (179 air on 14 tgt) or D.Wicks (171 air on 12). pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Burks went 13 again because WAS led wire-to-wire, handed Croskey-Merritt the ball, and the 225 air yards were two bombs that never got called — PHI's 23 explosives allowed were to other teams' WR1s, and a 4th-in-targets receiver (14 tgt, behind Okonkwo 17, Diggs 16, Williams 15) is exactly who a -5.5 favorite stops feeding. White cleared 58.5 the way he did in the 83 game: still a 14-carry back, not a healthy scratch, plus one checkdown drive like the 40-yard receiving game, and PHI's 4.32 YPC / 21 runs of 10+ turned a modest carry count into yards. Week 7 WAS usage was never in the L3 block, so the committee read was already stale by Sunday. The counter-case is real enough that both stay leans, not strongs, and neither is a price edge.
slip_story: One WAS usage story, not a shootout stack and not a PHI trailing stack: WAS controls a 23-17 type game, still takes one vertical shot to Burks (over 21.5 survives a run lean), and does not make White the closer (under 58.5). Do not add Goedert/Lemon overs, a White rush over, a Barkley rush over, or a game under — those need a different script. Two legs, no TDs. Correlation is only mild; a true WAS blowout helps White's under and can kill Burks.
